content.title: My Dream For South Africa - U.S. Embassy & Consulates in South Africa
content.text: My Dream For South Africa Essay & Speech Contest Earlier this year we launched the, “I Have a Dream for South Africa Speech & Essay Contest,” in honor of Martin Luther King Jr. and in celebration of 30 years of democracy in South Africa. The contest encouraged youth to share their dreams for South Africa, reflecting on democracy, equality, and social justice through compelling essays. In the spirit of democracy, we are giving you the chance to have a say. At the end of the introduction post series we will share over the coming weeks, we will open up voting on the U.S. Mission to South Africa’s website and will invite you to visit our site, read the essays, and choose your favorite contestant through our People’s Choice voting. Your vote will help determine which voices resonate most with South Africans across the country. Chuene Moabelo | Mpumalanga The Hope of a Nation “Remember that hope is a powerful weapon even when all else is lost,” said Nelson Mandela. I truly wish for this sentiment to be true or I fear for what is to become of our nation. Over the years, I have witnessed what I can only describe as a retrogression of our great country and its identity as a rainbow nation. Our fathers have forgotten how to be protectors, our mothers have forgotten how to use their voices, and the youth have lost their way without the leaders. Now they are forced to carry the burden of the heads. Day after day, we as a nation witness atrocities done to our fellow South Africans but remain silent without reason. Black-on-black violence has become the new trend of the decade and we Gen-Z are forced to develop under such violence and circumstances, even after the struggles of our forefathers. Our victory stemmed from unity and the desire for freedom, but now everyone desires to lead rather than follow. As a young adult, I yearn for hope. Hope for a better nation that protects both its citizens and immigrants. I want to believe in humanity once more, to trust my neighbor, and to take my children to the park without fear. I want my children to be able to dress however they please, to be seen as individuals rather than mere statistics, and to have faith in the justice system. Above all, I desire unity for the next generation. Looking ahead 30 years from now, I hope to witness substantial progress. I desire to see leaders who embody the qualities of true role models, representing and upholding the rights of the people. I envision a nation that is increasingly intelligent and selfless, acknowledging our history and using it as a tool to learn from past mistakes. Additionally, I firmly believe that complete transparency should be enforced. As citizens, we deserve to be informed about what is truly happening and have a voice in the matters that affect us. As a child of the African soil, I hope we can empathize with those affected by incompetent leadership. Let’s unite as one nation, inspired by our forefathers, to strive for what is best for all South Africans. Evan Rhys Powers | KwaZulu-Natal My dream for South Africa is woven with the threads of unity, equality, and purity as the founding fathers of a new country envisioned. The wounds of our country’s past have stopped bleeding, but the scars left behind will take a long time to heal. 30 years ago, in the new light of hope, our parents witnessed the dawning of the rising sun, tearing down 46 years of darkness in South Africa. The stories told to us are not generational, not far-fetched reaching back into the recollection of our ancestors… rather they are here, as close as sea is to our coastline, the mountains to our valleys. The hurt of the past still lingers to this day and can only be healed by looking to the future. So, the simple question to be asked is: what does the future hold for a country with its chains broken? The answer is simple, as you’ve been listening to them and their visions since the 19th of January. To stop hinting or being indirect, the future of South Africa is us; the youth. But the youth that you have heard from are the top 1% of the country. In 2021, 960 000 children had not received an education. How can we as a country weave a new South Africa if we have no threads to work together? 960 000 more threads could not only entwine a better South Africa, but a new one entirely. The future of South Africa hinges on empowering every South African with the education necessary to craft their own vision for our beautiful country. I want a South Africa smart enough to finish what the leaders of 1994 envisioned. We need a democratic resurgence and that can only come from the youth of today. A resurgence of a democracy that doesn’t pocket millions of rands into the accounts of corrupt leaders. A resurgence of a democracy that can lower our 32.1% unemployment rate. And finally, a resurgence of a democracy that can keep our lights on. The future of South Africa is not an idea or dream or vision, it is a people. And we can only lace together a new South Africa if each thread realizes their power and possibility in creating a South Africa of hope and prosperity. Hlumelo Mthuti | Western Cape A Dream for South Africa: Navigating the Path Forward As we commemorate Black History Month and reflect on 30 years of democracy in South Africa, it is essential to envision the future we aspire to create. In the words of Nelson Mandela, “Freedom cannot be achieved unless the women have been emancipated from all forms of oppression.” This statement underscores the importance of equality and inclusivity in our journey forward.In this essay, I will explore my dream for South Africa and outline the steps we must take to realize it. My vision is one of unity, equality, and opportunity for all, regardless of race, gender, or background. First and foremost, my dream for South Africa is a future where every individual is treated with dignity and respect. This means dismantling the barriers that perpetuate inequality and discrimination. It means ensuring that everyone has equal access to education, healthcare, and economic opportunities.Central to my vision is the principle of Ubuntu – the belief in a shared humanity and interconnectedness among all individuals. Ubuntu teaches us to recognize the inherent worth and dignity of every person and to embrace compassion and solidarity. In a society guided by Ubuntu, diversity is celebrated as a source of strength, and differences are seen as opportunities for growth and understanding. Furthermore, my dream for South Africa includes gender equality as a cornerstone of our society. Women must be empowered to participate fully in all aspects of life, from politics and business to education and healthcare. Gender-based violence must be eradicated, and women must be given the support and resources they need to thrive.To realize this dream, we must confront the challenges that continue to divide us as a nation. We must address the legacy of apartheid and work towards reconciliation and healing. We must tackle systemic issues such as poverty, unemployment, and corruption, which disproportionately affect marginalized communities. Education is key to unlocking the potential of our youth and building a brighter future for South Africa. We must invest in quality education that equips students with the skills and knowledge they need to succeed in the 21st century. This includes promoting STEM education, fostering critical thinking and creativity, and providing support for learners from disadvantaged backgroundsIn conclusion, my dream for South Africa is one of unity, equality, and opportunity for all. It is a future where the principles of Ubuntu guide our interactions, and where every individual has the chance to fulfill their potential. By working together and embracing our shared humanity, we can navigate the path forward and build a better tomorrow for generations to come. As we celebrate our past and look to the future, let us be guided by the words of Dr. King: “The time is always right to do what is right.” Together, we can build a South Africa that honors the sacrifices of the past, embraces the challenges of the present, and embraces the promise of a brighter tomorrow. Kutlo Motlhoioa | Northern Cape I wake up every morning filled with hope. I pridefully put on my uniform of faith and head into the school of dreams. Every classroom acts as a pending dream for South Africa. These doors open to classrooms full of opportunity and growth. I opened the door to the English class and observed the artists of change swaying their brushes of transformation. They are painting a picture of equal opportunity in our country. A canvas complete with diverse people, black, white and coloured, contributing towards a better tomorrow. Poets and writers in positions of power are busy making honest decisions that will ensure a higher quality of life for everyone. They have given voices to the poor in spirit. They have used their brushes of transformation to artfully pave the roads and erect hospitals and schools with enough capacity to accommodate everyone. Walking into the maths class, I noticed the prodigies hard at work. They have found solutions to the high unemployment rates and, by working together with the artists of opportunity, have found solutions that have helped the economy exponentially. They achieved this by creating jobs for the unemployed youth by providing them with skills and opportunities. They have built houses for the poor and have educated the generations of tomorrow who have found it hard to focus in the dark. However, these human calculators have found a way to generate megawatts to provide light for this ambitious youth. These future generations will have a better quality of life to sustain themselves and their children. As I walked into the physics class, I saw the scientists of progress who have calculated the powerful force of ubuntu that is constantly attracting everyone in our country. The force attracts all the good, repels all the bad, and creates an environment of peace and harmony. They have determined that the motion of nation-building is rapidly accelerating and achieving speeds greater than unity. Speeds of compassion. I opened the door to the history class and observed the young historians of the future. They admire the achievements of our past leaders. Acknowledging what they fought for and continuing the fight for peace, equality and love. They are determined to work together with the artists, mathematicians and physicists to help achieve the dream of a crime-free South Africa. At the end of the passage, I entered the door of the accounting class. I notice the leaders managing the nation’s resources with the highest integrity and transparency. They have ensured that every child receives the best education and quality of life by effectively distributing all the resources. These classrooms are accessible to anyone. This school of dreams accepts everyone, but only a few people find it. However, we are the engineers of this dream. We are the ones who will lay the foundation and make this school of dreams a reality. Oyama Dombela | Eastern Cape “I have a dream – where do we go from here?” As a 20-year-old girl growing up in South Africa, I dream of where democracy will take our nation in the next 30 years. Despite the difficulties that we confront, I am certain that with drive, innovative thinking, and solidarity, we can build a better future for all South Africans. First and foremost, I envision a South Africa in which every person can play a part in the democratic process. This includes ensuring that everyone has access to high-quality education, regardless of their socioeconomic status. Education is essential for creating opportunities and developing a trained workforce capable of driving economic development and innovation. Furthermore, I dream of a society in which variety is welcomed and appreciated. South Africa is a melting pot of cultures, languages, and customs, and we should represent this diversity in our institutions and leadership. By promoting inclusion and representation at all levels of government, we can guarantee that all South Africans’ perspectives are heard and respected. In addition, I believe that openness and accountability are critical components of a thriving democracy. We must hold our leaders accountable for their actions and choices, as well as keep government institutions free of corruption and nepotism. By creating a culture of honesty and trust, we can create a society that is fair and equitable for future generations. Furthermore, I envision South Africa becoming an innovator in technical innovation and sustainable development. By investing in renewable energy, green infrastructure, and eco-friendly activities, we can reduce the consequences of climate change and create a more resilient future for our world. Furthermore, embracing digitization and exploiting the power of technology may improve efficiency, connection, and access to information for all. I believe by then we would have worked on the problem of loadshedding because we have many upcoming young stars that think outside the box that can come up with good solutions for it the future. Lastly, I dream of a South Africa in which social justice and human rights are promoted and maintained. We must continue fight discrimination, inequalities, and injustice in all forms. By encouraging tolerance, empathy, and compassion, we may foster understanding and togetherness in our varied society. In conclusion, there are many obstacles in the path of our goal of a wealthier and more democratic South Africa, but my belief is that we can overcome them all if we band together and remain loyal to our principles. Let’s dare us to dream big and allow our acts of today mould the future we want for tomorrow. Zinhle Dube | Gauteng Prospects of Equitable Progress: A Vision for South Africa’s Nine Provinces in 2054 Introduction Ronald Reagan once said, “To sit back and hope that someday, someway, someone will make things right is like feeding the crocodile and hoping he will eat you last but eat you, he will.”(Wyeth, 2015) Promoting fair competition among South Africa’s nine provinces is a critical component of the country’s future strategy. A concentrated effort to level the playing field over the next 30 years will significantly mitigate the nation’s existing socioeconomic problems and create a more wealthy and balanced society. Equalizing Opportunities: The goal must be to reduce economic differences between the provinces to guarantee fair competition. This entails making calculated investments in healthcare, education, and infrastructure development to foster an atmosphere that supports economic expansion. Every province ought to be endowed with the ability to capitalize on its distinct advantages and make a significant contribution to the advancement of the country. Economic Diversification: Would it be best to provide incentives to vital companies like the automotive sector to promote growth within the Eastern Cape? Or would it be more prudent to use public funds to upgrade infrastructure or otherwise enhance the business climate for a range of industries? (Turok and Visagie, 2022). For inclusive and long-term growth, each province must promote economic diversification. Even if historically wealthy provinces continue to prosper, a stronger national economy could result from recognizing and maximizing the economic potential of impoverished areas. By attracting investments, generating jobs, and reducing reliance on industries, this diversity can improve resilience. Education and skills development: The high percentage of young people (32.4%) between the ages of 15 and 24 who are not in education, employment, or training (NEET) is partially caused by the inefficiency and ineffectiveness of PSET (Post-School Education and Training in South Africa). This is a worry for the nation because poor levels of education attainment and skill development are the main causes of intergenerational poverty, inequality, and youth unemployment in South Africa (Department of Planning, Monitoring and Evaluation, n.d.). Encouraging equal competition necessitates investing in education and skill development. The workforce gets more competent and adaptive when all provinces have access to high-quality education and training programs. A population with higher levels of education is better able to contribute to many areas of the economy, which promotes productivity and creativity. Conclusion South Africa could become a country where all provinces compete on an equal basis and contribute to the nation’s general socioeconomic well-being within the next thirty years. South Africa can create a future in which every person, regardless of where they live, has the chance to prosper by addressing social injustices, resolving economic inequality, encouraging education and skill development, and investing in infrastructure. The basis for a more cohesive, wealthy, and peaceful country is laid by this idea of fair competition. Anna Ramochela | Free State South Africa, with its rich history and diverse culture, has always been a land of dream and possibilities, despite its challenges, I harbour dreams and visions for a positive future that can transform the nation into a beacon of hope and prosperity. These dreams encapsulate aspirations for equality, opportunity, sustainability and unity, envisioning a South Africa that thrives on inclusivity and progress. At the heart of these dreams lies the fervent desire for equality and social justice. I envision future where every citizen, regardless of race, gender, or socio-economic background has equal access to opportunities and resources. This vision encompasses eradicating systematic inequalities, addressing historical injustices, and building a society where merit and hard work determine success rather than privilege. Education emerges as a cornerstone of this vision. I aspire a future where education is accessible to all, empowering individuals to realize their full potential and contribute meaningfully to society. Quality education, coupled with robust skills development programs holds the key to unlocking opportunities and breaking the cycle of poverty. In tandem with equality and education, sustainability forms an integral part of the collective vision for the future. Environmental stewardship, renewable energy initiatives, and conservation efforts are paramount in creating a south Africa that thrives in harmony with nature. Sustainable development practices ensure that future generations inherit thriving ecosystem and stable climate, fostering a legacy of environmental responsibility and resilience. moreover, economic prosperity features prominently is in one of my dreams. I aspire to cultivate an environment conducive to business development, job creation and investment fostering economic empowerment and reducing unemployment rates. A thriving economy not only lifts individuals out of poverty but also fosters a sense of pride and collective achievement. in essence the dreams and vision I have for positive future south Africa reflect a collective of yearning for society characterized by justice, opportunity, sustainability and unity. By embracing these dreams and working towards their realization, South Africa can indeed emerge as a shining example of resilience, progress, and possibility on the African continent beyond. Atlegang Moumakoe | North West My dream is to turn South Africa into a well developed and prosperous in the continent of Africa. One of my dreams include the involvement of youth in politics. I believe that youth can change the state of our country as they are more innovative and more advanced than the old generation that is leading the country now. For example, the parliament is full of the old generation who always lacks to accomplish the mission of upgrading South Africa. If more youth were to part-take in politics they will bring in more innovative ideas for the country. My dream also include change of leaders. I believe that changing the leaders of South Africa and replacing then with young blooded people can bring South Africa more innovative ways to rebuild it. I think that the leaders of South Africa have failed to lead South Africa in a reputable manner as to why there is a lot of corruption, crime and theft in this country and none of the parliament members are shaken of these major socio-economic issues. I dream of South Africa to be prosperous as other countries like Dubai, and I believe that we as South African citizens we can make it happen if only we join heads together and come up with ideas of how can South Africa change for the better. It takes one great mind to change the country for the best as it is always said that “great minds think alike “, I have hope that if we can join heads together we can come up with a good strategy on how to rebuild the country to become the prosperous country. Dr John Dermatini once said “ a master lives in the world of transformation, not in the world of loss and gain “. Lastly, I have a dream in the change of the education system. The education system of SA is very poor, I dream of South African citizens to be more advanced in terms of education so that they have more knowledge of the other concept of education, and this will reduce unemployment rate in SA as they will be highly educated. I conclude by saying our pride for our country should not come after our country becomes great but our country should become great because of our pride. Karabo Mpuru | Limpopo I have a dream. Where do we go from here? I have a dream. Where do we go from here? Three decades from now, how does it look? How does my country, the rainbow nation look? Thirty years ago prior to 1994; someone possibly might have wondered the same thing. They pondered on how life could look like, if things will ever change and when if not today. They were an eagle in a cage; the cage was the color of their skin. Filled with rage, determination and shear dedication they set into motion the long walk to freedom. It was supposed to be a peaceful protest- a satyagraha. However; along the way, it became a journey filled with bloodshed and tears, our home was a battle field where many courageous souls where laid to rest. They were Nelson Mandela. And after 27 years in another cage, isolated on an island; freedom was granted. But despite our country having freedom, its people did not have equal freedom. Now, three decades into 1994, its 2024; I have a dream. Where we go from here are destinations beyond our dreams. Where we reach new heights and advance at accelerating speeds. We go to a home where corruption is abolished and rights are acknowledged and enforced with of course the appropriate responsibilities applying. A home of diversity without adversity, where everyone is equally, loved, heard and most importantly feels safe. I’m taking about all women: young and old, and children who are the bearers of our future feeling safe. I am talking about having free universal healthcare and emotional support to both women and men. Schools being a place to learn instead of an escape from unbearable circumstances at home. Our country using green energy and giving back to the environment, by using ecofriendly materials when building and re furbishing old cities. A rise in leadership from the youth worldwide, with the youth using the resources they have such as technology to reach many ears and spread hope to others. Though there are many obstacles that may come, we, as a nation have taken the first step towards achieving absolute excellence; such as overcoming apartheid and helping other countries to fight apartheid. We continue to take many more steps, with each step we leave a mark, an impact, an impression in history, and we continue to grow exponentially, beating every odd and succeeding.
